---
name: blueprint-conventions
description: The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs.
---

Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.

## Environments

Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
its following `proof` environment form one node's content.

## Per-node macros

- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration(s) this node formalizes; comma-separate to
  bind several (`\lean{a, b}`) when they jointly formalize the node's statement.
  Each named declaration's signature must match the statement. The mapping need
  not be 1-to-1: a node may name several declarations, and Lean may carry
  auxiliary declarations with no node at all.
- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
  proof.
- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).
- `\notready` — the Lean is **not written yet**: the node's statement stands but
  no declaration formalizes it. Mutually exclusive with `\leanok` (a node is
  never both) — remove `\notready` exactly when you add `\leanok`, i.e. the
  moment its Lean is written and checked. It is a human-facing marker of an
  intentional gap, not a DAG edge.

## House style

- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
  and no conversational filler. Not every Lean helper needs its own node —
  auxiliary or implementation-only declarations can stay unnoded; add a node when
  the result is mathematically meaningful in its own right. In particular, never
  add a `Formalization note` paragraph to blueprint `.tex`: attach implementation
  details, failed approaches, and mechanization caveats to the statement's hgraph
  node with `horizon graph ... add comment` instead.
- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
  its proof stays complete.
- **One statement's worth per node.** Keep each node to a single mathematical
  statement; don't restate Lean source as prose.
- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

 10656	  \(x_i = \langle a_i, \xi_i \rangle\) of \(\Sigma\)-elements.
 10657	
 10658	  \emph{Structure components.} Compatibility on pullbacks forces the \(a_i\) to agree on
 10659	  overlaps, so they glue to a unique \(a_Y \colon Y \to \Spec k\) with
 10660	  \(\iota_i \circ a_Y = a_i\) (gluing of scheme morphisms along an open cover).
 10661	
 10662	  \emph{Fibre components.} The cover members induce slice morphisms
 10663	  \((U_i, a_i) \to (Y, a_Y)\) with open-immersion left legs and jointly surjective ranges.
 10664	  The fibres \(\xi_i\) are a compatible family on this slice cover: by the compatibility
 10665	  descent (Lemma~\ref{lem:sigmaExtension_seams}(iii)), the \(\Sigma\)-level compatibility of
 10666	  the \(x_i\) descends to slice-level compatibility of the \(\xi_i\). By the morphism-form
 10667	  sheaf property of the degree-zero functor
 10668	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover}) the \(\xi_i\) glue to a unique
 10669	  degree-zero class \(s\) on \((Y, a_Y)\) restricting to each.
 10670	
 10671	  \emph{Stitching.} The \(\Sigma\)-element \(\langle a_Y, s\rangle\) restricts to each
 10672	  \(x_i\) by the amalgamation seam (Lemma~\ref{lem:sigmaExtension_seams}(i)). Uniqueness:
 10673	  the structure component of any amalgamation is determined by gluing of morphisms, and its
 10674	  fibre by the separation half of
 10675	  Theorem~\ref{thm:pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover}, again through the seam.
 10676	\end{proof}

 10678	\begin{definition}[Local representability descends to the slice]
 10679	  \label{def:pic0RepresentableByOfCharts}
 10680	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts}
 10681	  \uses{thm:pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf, thm:representableBy_overSlice, def:pic0SigmaFunctor}
 10682	  \leanok
 10683	  Suppose given a family of schemes \(X_i\) with maps
 10684	  \(f_i \colon \mathrm{yoneda}(X_i) \to \widetilde{\mathrm{pic}^0}(C)\) of big-site sheaves
 10685	  which are relatively representable open immersions, jointly Zariski-locally surjective.
 10686	  Then the local-representability theorem glues the \(X_i\) into a scheme \(J\)
 10687	  representing the \(\Sigma\)-extension, and by \(\Sigma\)-descent
 10688	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:representableBy_overSlice}) the set-valued degree-zero Picard functor is
 10689	  representable on the slice by \(J\) placed over \(\Spec k\) via the structure component of
 10690	  the universal element.
 10691	\end{definition}

 10693	  \leanok
 10694	  The local-representability theorem for Zariski sheaves on schemes (mathlib's
 10695	  01JJ engine) applies to the sheaf of Theorem~\ref{thm:pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf} and the
 10696	  given chart family, producing a representation of the \(\Sigma\)-extension by the glued
 10697	  scheme; compose with Theorem~\ref{thm:representableBy_overSlice}.
 10698	\end{proof}

 10700	This remains a valid conditional local-representability theorem. Spelled out, its hypothesis
 10701	asks for a family of schemes \(X_i\) together
 10702	with maps \(\mathrm{yoneda}(X_i) \to \widetilde{\mathrm{pic}^0}(C)\) such that
 10703	
 10704	\begin{itemize}
 10705	  \item each \(f_i\) is \emph{relatively representable by an open immersion}: for every
 10706	    scheme \(T\) and every \(\Sigma\)-element \(\xi \in \widetilde{\mathrm{pic}^0}(C)(T)\),
 10707	    the fibre product \(\mathrm{yoneda}(X_i) \times_{\widetilde{\mathrm{pic}^0}(C)} T\) is
 10708	    representable by an open subscheme of \(T\) --- so each \(f_i\) exhibits \(X_i\) as an
 10709	    \emph{open piece} of the functor, with the openness verified at every test, not merely
 10710	    at points;
 10711	  \item the family is \emph{jointly Zariski-locally surjective}: every element of
 10712	    \(\widetilde{\mathrm{pic}^0}(C)(T)\) is, after restriction to the members of some open
 10713	    cover of \(T\), in the image of some \(f_i\).
 10714	\end{itemize}
 10715	
 10716	These hypotheses are not supplied by the raw admissible Abel map. Its fibres are complete
 10717	linear systems and can have positive dimension, so that map cannot be an open immersion or
 10718	an open atlas. The representability producer pursued here is instead the corrected
 10719	Altman--Kleiman construction of Section~\ref{sec:admissibleAbelQuotient}: represent the
 10720	kernel relation of the unconditional widened divisor source, form its effective quotient,
 10721	and identify the quotient Yoneda sheaf with the degree-zero Picard functor. The auxiliary
 10722	fixed-window Theorem~\ref{thm:divRepUniversalFamily} is not an obstruction to the already
 10723	landed widened representation and is not the endpoint's missing input.

 10725	\section{The Abel element}
 10726	\label{sec:abelElement}
 10727	
 10728	For a rational point \(P\) of the curve, the class of the diagonal minus the constant graph
 10729	is a degree-zero family on the test \(T = C\) — the element whose image under the universal
 10730	correspondence of the representation is the Abel map.
 10731	
 10732	\begin{theorem}[The unit seam at arbitrary tests]
 10733	  \label{thm:degAt_relPicToPicEt}
 10734	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_relPicToPicEt}
 10735	  \uses{def:degAt, thm:picEtMap_relPicToPicEt, thm:picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt,
 10736	    thm:degAff_unit, def:relPicToPicEt, def:relPicMap}
 10737	  \leanok
 10738	  For a test object \(T\), a relative Picard class \(z \in \mathrm{relPic}(C,T)\) and a
 10739	  field point \(t \colon \Spec K \to T\), the degree at \(t\) of the unit image of \(z\) is
 10740	  the relative degree of the restriction:
 10741	  \[
 10742	    \deg_t\bigl(\mathrm{relPicToPicEt}(z)\bigr) = \mathrm{relPicDeg}_K\bigl(t^{*} z\bigr).
 10743	  \]
 10744	\end{theorem}
 10745	\begin{proof}
 10746	  \leanok
 10747	  Naturality of the unit (Theorem~\ref{thm:picEtMap_relPicToPicEt}) collapses the
 10748	  restriction along \(t\) to the unit image of \(t^{*}z\) over \(\Spec K\); affine
 10749	  consistency (Theorem~\ref{thm:picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt}) identifies its affine
 10750	  collapse with the plus unit of \(t^{*}z\); the unit normalization of the degree
 10751	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:degAff_unit}) reads \(\mathrm{relPicDeg}_K\).
 10752	\end{proof}
 10753	
 10754	\begin{definition}[The Abel \v Cech class]
 10755	  \label{def:abelCechClass}
 10756	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.abelCechClass, AlgebraicGeometry.abelPicEt}
 10757	  \uses{def:graphLocalEquations, def:relPicToPicEt, def:relPic}
 10758	  \leanok
 10759	  \source{kleiman-picard, abelian-varieties:page-0107}
 10760	  Let \(P \colon \mathbf{1} \to C\) be a rational point of the curve (a morphism from the
 10761	  unit test). The \emph{Abel \v Cech class} on the test \(T = C\) is
 10762	  \[
 10763	    \mathcal A_P \;:=\; \struct{C \otimes C}(\Delta) \cdot \struct{C \otimes C}(P \times C)^{-1}
 10764	      \;\in\; \Pic(C \otimes C),
 10765	  \]
 10766	  the graph class of the identity \(\id_C\) (the diagonal) times the inverse graph class of
 10767	  the constant point \(C \to \mathbf 1 \xrightarrow{P} C\) — both factors through the graph
 10768	  divisor of Definition~\ref{def:graphLocalEquations}, so one degree certificate serves
 10769	  both. The \emph{Abel class} \(\alpha_P \in \mathrm{picEt}(C, C)\) is the unit image of its
 10770	  relative class. Milne's cited section assumes \(g(C)>0\); this graph-class construction
 10771	  uses only the rational point \(P\) and therefore also applies in genus zero.
 10772	\end{definition}
 10773	
 10774	\begin{theorem}[The functor-point formula, \v Cech level]
 10775	  \label{thm:cechPicMap_abelCechClass}
 10776	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.cechPicMap_abelCechClass}
 10777	  \uses{def:abelCechClass, thm:graphLocalEquations_base_change}
 10778	  \leanok
 10779	  For any test \(T\) and any point \(f \colon T \to C\), the pullback of the Abel \v Cech
 10780	  class along \(C \lhd f\) is the graph-minus-constant-graph class of \(f\):
 10781	  \[
 10782	    (C \lhd f)^{*} \mathcal A_P
 10783	      = \struct{C \otimes T}(\Gamma_f)\cdot\struct{C \otimes T}(\Gamma_{P_T})^{-1},
 10784	  \]
 10785	  where \(P_T \colon T \to \mathbf 1 \xrightarrow{P} C\) is the constant point of \(T\).
 10786	\end{theorem}
 10787	\begin{proof}
 10788	  \leanok
 10789	  Base change of the graph class (Theorem~\ref{thm:graphLocalEquations_base_change}) sends
 10790	  \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{\id_C})\) to \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{f \circ \id}) = \struct{}(\Gamma_f)\)
 10791	  and \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{P_C})\) to \(\struct{}(\Gamma_{f \circ P_C})\); and
 10792	  \(f \circ P_C = P_T\) by terminality of the unit test (both factor through
 10793	  \(\mathbf 1\)). Pullback is a homomorphism, so the product formula follows.
 10794	\end{proof}

 10678	\begin{definition}[Local representability descends to the slice]
 10679	  \label{def:pic0RepresentableByOfCharts}
 10680	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts}
 10681	  \uses{thm:pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf, thm:representableBy_overSlice, def:pic0SigmaFunctor}
 10682	  \leanok
 10683	  Suppose given a family of schemes \(X_i\) with maps
 10684	  \(f_i \colon \mathrm{yoneda}(X_i) \to \widetilde{\mathrm{pic}^0}(C)\) of big-site sheaves
 10685	  which are relatively representable open immersions, jointly Zariski-locally surjective.
 10686	  Then the local-representability theorem glues the \(X_i\) into a scheme \(J\)
 10687	  representing the \(\Sigma\)-extension, and by \(\Sigma\)-descent
 10688	  (Theorem~\ref{thm:representableBy_overSlice}) the set-valued degree-zero Picard functor is
 10689	  representable on the slice by \(J\) placed over \(\Spec k\) via the structure component of
 10690	  the universal element.
 10691	\end{definition}
 10692	\begin{proof}
 10693	  \leanok
 10694	  The local-representability theorem for Zariski sheaves on schemes (mathlib's
 10695	  01JJ engine) applies to the sheaf of Theorem~\ref{thm:pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf} and the
 10696	  given chart family, producing a representation of the \(\Sigma\)-extension by the glued
 10697	  scheme; compose with Theorem~\ref{thm:representableBy_overSlice}.
 10698	\end{proof}
 10699	
 10700	This remains a valid conditional local-representability theorem. Spelled out, its hypothesis
 10701	asks for a family of schemes \(X_i\) together
 10702	with maps \(\mathrm{yoneda}(X_i) \to \widetilde{\mathrm{pic}^0}(C)\) such that
 10703	
 10704	\begin{itemize}
 10705	  \item each \(f_i\) is \emph{relatively representable by an open immersion}: for every
 10706	    scheme \(T\) and every \(\Sigma\)-element \(\xi \in \widetilde{\mathrm{pic}^0}(C)(T)\),
 10707	    the fibre product \(\mathrm{yoneda}(X_i) \times_{\widetilde{\mathrm{pic}^0}(C)} T\) is
 10708	    representable by an open subscheme of \(T\) --- so each \(f_i\) exhibits \(X_i\) as an
 10709	    \emph{open piece} of the functor, with the openness verified at every test, not merely
 10710	    at points;
 10711	  \item the family is \emph{jointly Zariski-locally surjective}: every element of
 10712	    \(\widetilde{\mathrm{pic}^0}(C)(T)\) is, after restriction to the members of some open
 10713	    cover of \(T\), in the image of some \(f_i\).
 10714	\end{itemize}
 10715	
 10716	These hypotheses are not supplied by the raw admissible Abel map. Its fibres are complete
 10717	linear systems and can have positive dimension, so that map cannot be an open immersion or
 10718	an open atlas. The representability producer pursued here is instead the corrected
 10719	Altman--Kleiman construction of Section~\ref{sec:admissibleAbelQuotient}: represent the
 10720	kernel relation of the unconditional widened divisor source, form its effective quotient,
 10721	and identify the quotient Yoneda sheaf with the degree-zero Picard functor. The auxiliary
 10722	fixed-window Theorem~\ref{thm:divRepUniversalFamily} is not an obstruction to the already
 10723	landed widened representation and is not the endpoint's missing input.

 10725	\section{The Abel element}

     9	/-!
    10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor on all test objects: the object level
    11	
    12	For a curve `C` over `k`, the étale-sheafified relative Picard group of an **affine**
    13	test is the one-step plus construction `PicEtAff C A` (étale-separatedness of the
    14	relative Picard presheaf makes one plus suffice — axiom (C1),
    15	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.CechKernelLemma`).  The frozen group-object interface forces
    16	the functor to exist on **all** of `Over (Spec k)`; following the resolution of the
    17	Layer-2 vehicle question (inbox I-0140), the extension is the *bespoke affine-opens
    18	limit*: a section over a test object `T` is a compatible family of plus classes over the
    19	affine opens of `T.left`, valued in `PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U)` via the section-ring
    20	algebras of `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtSections`.  The index poset is `Type u`-small,
    21	which is the point of the vehicle.
    22	
    23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEt C T`: the limit, as the subgroup of the product over
    24	  `T.left.affineOpens` cut out by compatibility under restriction, with its `CommGroup`
    25	  structure; `picEt.eval` is evaluation at an affine open.
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.congr C e`: transport of plus classes along an isomorphism
    27	  of test algebras.
    28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtAffineEquiv C A`: **the affine comparison** — on an affine
    29	  test `overSpec k A`, evaluation at the top affine open is a group isomorphism
    30	  `picEt C (overSpec k A) ≃* PicEtAff C A` (the affine-opens poset of an affine test has
    31	  a terminal element, so the limit collapses).
    32	
    33	Functoriality in `T` — restriction along an arbitrary morphism of test objects, by
    34	gluing over basic-open refinements, licensed by (C1)-separatedness — is built on top of
    35	the Zariski sheaf property of `PicEtAff` in `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap`.
    36	-/
    37	
    38	set_option autoImplicit false
    39	
    40	universe u
    41	
    42	open CategoryTheory
    43	
    44	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    45	
    46	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    47	
    48	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra
    49	
    50	noncomputable section
    51	
    52	/-! ## Transport of plus classes along an isomorphism of test algebras -/
    53	
    54	namespace PicEtAff
    55	
    56	variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    57	
    58	/-- Transport of étale-plus Picard classes along an isomorphism of test algebras. -/
    59	def congr (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) : PicEtAff C A ≃* PicEtAff C B where
    60	  toFun := mapAlg C e.toAlgHom
    61	  invFun := mapAlg C e.symm.toAlgHom
    62	  left_inv x := by
    63	    rw [← mapAlg_comp, show (e.symm.toAlgHom.comp e.toAlgHom) = AlgHom.id k A from
    64	      AlgHom.ext fun a => e.symm_apply_apply a]
    65	    exact mapAlg_id C x
    66	  right_inv x := by
    67	    rw [← mapAlg_comp, show (e.toAlgHom.comp e.symm.toAlgHom) = AlgHom.id k B from
    68	      AlgHom.ext fun b => e.apply_symm_apply b]
    69	    exact mapAlg_id C x
    70	  map_mul' x y := map_mul (mapAlg C e.toAlgHom) x y
    71	
    72	@[simp]
    73	lemma congr_apply (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) (x : PicEtAff C A) :
    74	    congr C e x = mapAlg C e.toAlgHom x :=
    75	  rfl
    76	
    77	@[simp]
    78	lemma congr_symm_apply (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) (x : PicEtAff C B) :
    79	    (congr C e).symm x = mapAlg C e.symm.toAlgHom x :=
    80	  rfl
    81	
    82	end PicEtAff
    83	
    84	/-! ## The affine-opens limit -/
    85	
    86	variable (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    87	
    88	/-- The compatible families over the affine opens of the test object, as a subgroup of
    89	the product of the affine-level plus groups: the value at a smaller affine open is the
    90	restriction of the value at a larger one. -/
    91	def picEtSubgroup :
    92	    Subgroup (Π U : T.left.affineOpens, PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1)) where
    93	  carrier := {s | ∀ (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1),
    94	    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s V) = s U}
    95	  one_mem' := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one]
    96	  mul_mem' {a b} ha hb := fun U V h => by
    97	    rw [Pi.mul_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, ha U V h, hb U V h]
    98	  inv_mem' {a} ha := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.inv_apply, Pi.inv_apply, map_inv, ha U V h]
    99	
   100	/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor at an arbitrary test object**, object
   101	level: compatible families of affine-level plus classes over the affine opens of
   102	`T.left` — the bespoke affine-opens limit of `PicEtAff C ∘ Γ(T.left, ·)`.  On affine
   103	tests this is `PicEtAff` itself (`picEtAffineEquiv`); on general tests it is its
   104	canonical Zariski-continuous extension. -/
   105	def picEt : Type u :=
   106	  picEtSubgroup C T
   107	
   108	noncomputable instance : CommGroup (picEt C T) :=
   109	  inferInstanceAs (CommGroup (picEtSubgroup C T))
   110	
   111	namespace picEt
   112	
   113	variable {C T}
   114	
   115	/-- The compatibility of a section of `picEt` along an inclusion of affine opens. -/
   116	lemma compat (s : picEt C T) (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1) :
   117	    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s.1 V) = s.1 U :=
   118	  s.2 U V h
   119	
   120	@[ext]
   121	lemma ext {s t : picEt C T} (h : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens, s.1 U = t.1 U) : s = t :=
   122	  Subtype.ext (funext h)
   123	
   124	variable (C T) in
   125	/-- Evaluation of a section of `picEt` at an affine open, as a group homomorphism. -/
   126	def eval (U : T.left.affineOpens) : picEt C T →* PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1) :=
   127	  (Pi.evalMonoidHom (fun V : T.left.affineOpens => PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, V.1)) U).comp
   128	    (picEtSubgroup C T).subtype
   129	
   130	@[simp]
   131	lemma eval_apply (U : T.left.affineOpens) (s : picEt C T) : eval C T U s = s.1 U :=
   132	  rfl
   133	
   134	@[simp]
   135	lemma mul_val (s t : picEt C T) (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
   136	    (s * t).1 U = s.1 U * t.1 U :=
   137	  rfl
   138	
   139	@[simp]
   140	lemma one_val (U : T.left.affineOpens) : (1 : picEt C T).1 U = 1 :=
   141	  rfl
   142	
   143	@[simp]
   144	lemma inv_val (s : picEt C T) (U : T.left.affineOpens) : (s⁻¹).1 U = (s.1 U)⁻¹ :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	end picEt
   148	
   149	/-! ## The affine comparison -/
   150	
   151	section Affine
   152	
   153	variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   154	
   155	/-- The top affine open of an affine test object. -/
   156	def overSpecTopAffine : (overSpec k A).left.affineOpens :=
   157	  ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top_overSpec k A⟩
   158	
   159	/-- Evaluation at the top affine open of an affine test, composed with the
   160	`ΓSpecIso`-transport into the test algebra: the forward direction of the affine
   161	comparison. -/
   162	def picEtToAff : picEt C (overSpec k A) →* PicEtAff C A :=
   163	  (PicEtAff.congr C (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A)).toMonoidHom.comp
   164	    (picEt.eval C (overSpec k A) (overSpecTopAffine A))
   165	
   166	lemma picEtToAff_apply (s : picEt C (overSpec k A)) :
   167	    picEtToAff C A s
   168	      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom
   169	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) :=
   170	  rfl
   171	
   172	/-- The section of `picEt` over an affine test determined by a plus class of the test
   173	algebra: restrict from the top affine open — the inverse direction of the affine
   174	comparison. -/
   175	def picEtOfAff : PicEtAff C A →* picEt C (overSpec k A) where
   176	  toFun x :=
   177	    ⟨fun U => PicEtAff.mapAlg C
   178	      ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp
   179	        (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom) x,
   180	      fun U V h => by rw [← PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp, ← AlgHom.comp_assoc,
   181	        Over.resAlgHom_comp]⟩
   182	  map_one' := picEt.ext fun U => map_one (PicEtAff.mapAlg C _)
   183	  map_mul' x y := picEt.ext fun U => map_mul (PicEtAff.mapAlg C _) x y
   184	
   185	lemma picEtOfAff_val (x : PicEtAff C A) (U : (overSpec k A).left.affineOpens) :
   186	    (picEtOfAff C A x).1 U
   187	      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C
   188	          ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp
   189	            (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom) x :=
   190	  rfl

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusOpen
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusFibreField

/-!
# The class-indexed witness locus and its openness (the untwisted predecessor of `chartLocus`)

`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusOpen.lean` proves openness of the witness locus of a *chosen*
basic-open cocycle datum `D`; `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean` proves that the witness
predicate is intrinsic to the *fibre class* of the datum.  Both are stated per datum.  This
file makes the step neither takes: it indexes the locus by a **class**.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.cechWitnessLocus π c` — `{q : Spec B | every basic-open cocycle datum
  with fibre class `c` has an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹` at `κ(q)`}`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_of_datum` — any ONE presenting datum is a
  sound and complete test (class-intrinsicity).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists` — the ∀-form and the ∃-form agree
  (every class is presented, `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_cechWitnessLocus` — the openness.

## THIS IS NOT `chartLocus`, AND NOT `isOpen_chartLocus`

Those two names are RESERVED, and co-signed between two lanes: `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md`
§3.3 (CHART-U(a)) freezes `chartLocus c λ` for a locus over a general test `T`, indexed by a
**plus class** `λ ∈ pic0Subgroup C (Over.mk a)`, at the **twisted** fibre class
`λ_t · θ^m · (−Σ)`; `informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6 co-signs it with two binding
amendments — the predicate for arbitrary plus classes is the SPLIT form over a finite
separable `L/κ(t)`, and the openness route of record is a three-transport chain — and row B-4
owns `isOpen_chartLocus` as the *assembly* of DAT-B's transports (i)/(ii) against DAT-C's
shifted-datum half.  None of that is here.

What IS here is the step those amendments presuppose and nobody had written: over an affine
base, for an UNTWISTED `CechPic` class, the engine's per-datum output is a locus of the class.
Call it transport (0).  Still missing for `chartLocus` proper: the shifted-datum constructor
(DAT-C GAP-1 — no `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.mul`/tensor exists), the split predicate
(a-amendment), and transports (i) descent and (ii) étale image (DAT-B).

Free of the DD-R certificate lane and of `divRep`: no `DivFamZar`, no `IsCertified`, no
`RepresentableBy` datum appears in the cone.
-/
set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
open TopologicalSpace Opposite

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open AlgebraicJacobian

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

variable (π) in
/-- **The witness locus of an untwisted class over an affine base**: the set of points of
`Spec B` at which the fibre of the Čech class `c` admits an effective witness divisor with
vanishing `H¹`.

Stated over *classes*, not over data: a basic-open cocycle datum is a presentation, and the
campaign's consumers index charts by a Picard class.  The ∀-quantifier is harmless because
the predicate is class-intrinsic
(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq`) and every class is
presented (`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`) — see
`mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists`.

NOT the co-signed `chartLocus c λ` of `w4-datc` §3.3 / `w4-datb` §1.6: that one lives over a
general test, is indexed by a plus class, and reads the TWISTED fibre class.  See the module
header. -/
def cechWitnessLocus (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) : Set (PrimeSpectrum B) :=
  {q : PrimeSpectrum B | ∀ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
    D.cechPicClass = c → D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField}

theorem mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    q ∈ cechWitnessLocus π c ↔ ∀ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
      D.cechPicClass = c → D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- **Membership is testable at any one presentation**: a datum `D` presenting `c` is a
sound and complete test for membership of the witness locus.  This is the class-intrinsicity
of the witness predicate, `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq`, in the form
the consumers use. -/
theorem mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_of_datum {c : (relCurve C B).CechPic}
    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hD : D.cechPicClass = c) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    q ∈ cechWitnessLocus π c ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField := by
  refine ⟨fun h => h D hD, fun h D' hD' => ?_⟩
  refine (D'.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq D
    q.asIdeal.ResidueField ?_).mpr h
  exact congrArg (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    (hD'.trans hD.symm)

/-- **The ∀-form and the ∃-form of the witness locus agree**: every class is presented by
some datum, and the witness predicate does not depend on which. -/
theorem mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    q ∈ cechWitnessLocus π c ↔ ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
      D.cechPicClass = c ∧ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField := by
  obtain ⟨D₀, hD₀⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (π := π) c
  refine ⟨fun h => ⟨D₀, hD₀, h D₀ hD₀⟩, fun ⟨D, hD, h⟩ => ?_⟩
  exact (mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_of_datum D hD q).mpr h

/-- **The class-indexed witness locus is open**: it is the witness locus of any one
presenting datum, and that is open by
`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing` (the audited,
Noetherian-free openness engine).

This is the first *datum-choice-free* openness statement in the campaign — the engine output
is stated for a chosen `D`, which is not something a locus indexed by a Picard class may
depend on.  It is strictly weaker than the reserved `isOpen_chartLocus` (dat-b row B-4),
which assembles this with the shifted-datum constructor and the descent/étale-image
transports; do not cite it as that. -/
theorem isOpen_cechWitnessLocus (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) : IsOpen (cechWitnessLocus π c) := by
  obtain ⟨D₀, hD₀⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (π := π) c
  have hset : cechWitnessLocus π c
      = {q : PrimeSpectrum B |
          ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
                = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField)
                    D₀.cechPicClass
              ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
                  ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
                    q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} :=
    Set.ext fun q => mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_of_datum D₀ hD₀ q
  rw [hset]
  exact D₀.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing hπ

end AlgebraicGeometry

name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
  named obligation open.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorDatumRankOne
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0VanishingFieldTest
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# THE RIGID ENGINE FIRES AT GENUS `0` ON A FIBREWISE-TRIVIAL CLASS, OVER A TEST RING
    11	
    12	`Picard/Pic0VanishingFieldTest.lean` closed every **field** instance of the degree-zero
    13	Picard vanishing at genus `0`; `Picard/Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean` proved the `∀ T`
    14	binder *is* the `∀` test-ring binder.  What remained was the **ring** case, and the note
    15	released with it priced that as "cohomology and base change, absent from this tree".
    16	
    17	**That price was wrong, and this file is the correction.**  The relevant engine is landed and
    18	is stated over an arbitrary test ring for an arbitrary class:
    19	
    20	* `Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301` — every Čech Picard class on `C_B` is
    21	  `D.cechPicClass` for some `BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π`, at **every** `k`-algebra `B`;
    22	* `Cohomology/GluedSheafEngine.lean:198` — `datumRigidEngine`: from a *fibrewise* `H¹`
    23	  hypothesis, `H¹(C_B, F_D) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F_D)` is finite projective over `B`;
    24	* `Cohomology/GluedSheafDatumFibre.lean:169` — the fibrewise hypothesis follows from a
    25	  witness divisor on the fibre curve with vanishing `H¹`;
    26	* `Picard/DivisorDatumRankOne.lean:148` — on the vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` and
    27	  `χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`, the stalk rank of `H⁰` is `1`.
    28	
    29	What nobody had connected is that at **genus `0`** the fibre inputs of that chain are *free*
    30	rather than expensive, and this file proves exactly that.
    31	
    32	## The two results, and why the hypothesis is the cheap one
    33	
    34	The fibre witness is the **zero divisor**.  Its class is `1` (`picClass_zero`) and its sheaf is
    35	the structure sheaf (`moduleKSheafDivisorSheafZeroIso`), whose `H¹` has `K`-dimension
    36	`genus C` at every field extension `K/k` (`finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus`) — so at genus `0` it
    37	vanishes, at every prime of `B` at once, with no locus, no openness argument and no
    38	spreading-out.  Hence:
    39	
    40	* `subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero` — the engine's `hfib` clause, for **any**
    41	  datum whose fibre classes are trivial;
    42	* `rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_genus_zero` — `H⁰` of stalk rank `1` at every prime,
    43	  i.e. `π_*L` invertible in the rank spelling, with `χ = 1` supplied by `genus C = 0` rather
    44	  than assumed.
    45	
    46	**The hypothesis is fibre-class triviality, not fibre degree.**  That spelling is deliberate
    47	and is not a strengthening in disguise: at genus `0` the two are *equivalent* by the landed
    48	field-level converse (`eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one`), and
    49	`fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` below is that equivalence at this site.  The
    50	reason to state the theorems on triviality is mechanical, and worth recording because it will
    51	bite the next lane: `classDeg K` carries five instance binders on the fibre curve
    52	(`IsIntegral`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `QuasiCompact`, and both `Module.Finite`
    53	Betti-number clauses) which do not synthesize through the `relCurve` `def` barrier, so a
    54	hypothesis phrased `∀ p, classDeg κ(p) … = 0` **cannot be stated** at a general prime without
    55	`haveI`-installing them first — measured, not guessed.  Triviality of the class needs none of
    56	them.
    57	
    58	## What this does NOT do
    59	
    60	* **It does not discharge the `pic⁰` vanishing at a test ring.**  It supplies the two
    61	  cohomological outputs — `H¹ = 0` and `H⁰` invertible — that the classical proof consumes
    62	  next through the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`.
    63	
    64	  **CORRECTED after a fresh-context audit (`I-1651`).**  An earlier version of this bullet said
    65	  that map "does not exist in this tree, in the sibling project, or in mathlib (measured this
    66	  session)".  **The mathlib half was false and unmeasured**: the map is the counit of
    67	  `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction`
    68	  (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Sheaf.lean`), and the sibling project applies
    69	  `.counit.app` to it in two files.  What is genuinely absent is any theorem saying that counit
    70	  is an **isomorphism** at a sheaf of this kind — that is the real residue, and it is a
    71	  narrower and more defensible claim than the one this bullet used to make.  AJCR's own
    72	  carriers are `Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (ModuleCat R)`, not `Scheme.Modules`, so
    73	  reaching the counit here is itself a port.
    74	* **It says nothing at positive genus**, where the fibre `H¹` is genuinely nonzero and the
    75	  witness above fails at the first step.
    76	* It introduces **no hypothesis on the curve** beyond the three standing binders and
    77	  `genus C = 0`, and no hypothesis on the test ring beyond `IsNoetherianRing` — which
    78	  `Cohomology/DatumDescent.lean:547` is designed to remove and which a consumer should remove
    79	  through that route rather than by re-proving anything here.
    80	
    81	## Main declarations
    82	
    83	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero`
    84	  — **the engine's fibrewise hypothesis, free at genus `0`**.
    85	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rigidEngine_of_genus_zero` — the engine's three
    86	  conclusions with the fibrewise clause discharged.
    87	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_genus_zero` —
    88	  **`H⁰` of stalk rank `1`**, at every prime.
    89	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` — the
    90	  degree-`0` spelling of the hypothesis implies the triviality spelling, so nothing is lost by
    91	  stating the results on the latter.
    92	-/

   148	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0) (p : PrimeSpectrum B)

lemma image_top : (⊤ : Subfunctor F).image f = range f := by aesop

@[simp]
lemma image_iSup {ι : Type*} (G : ι → Subfunctor F) (f : F ⟶ F') :
    (⨆ i, G i).image f = ⨆ i, (G i).image f := by aesop

lemma image_comp (g : F' ⟶ F'') :
    G.image (f ≫ g) = (G.image f).image g := by aesop

lemma range_comp (g : F' ⟶ F'') :
    range (f ≫ g) = (range f).image g := by aesop

end image

section preimage

/-- The preimage of a subfunctor by a morphism of type-valued functors. -/
@[simps]
def preimage (G : Subfunctor F) (p : F' ⟶ F) : Subfunctor F' where
  obj n := p.app n ⁻¹' (G.obj n)
  map f := (Set.preimage_mono (G.map f)).trans (by
    simp only [Set.preimage_preimage, NatTrans.naturality_apply]
    rfl)

@[simp]
lemma preimage_id (G : Subfunctor F) :
    G.preimage (𝟙 F) = G := by aesop

lemma preimage_comp (G : Subfunctor F) (f : F'' ⟶ F') (g : F' ⟶ F) :
    G.preimage (f ≫ g) = (G.preimage g).preimage f := by aesop

lemma image_le_iff (G : Subfunctor F) (f : F ⟶ F') (G' : Subfunctor F') :
    G.image f ≤ G' ↔ G ≤ G'.preimage f := by
  simp [Subfunctor.le_def]

/-- Given a morphism `p : F' ⟶ F` of type-valued functors and `G : Subfunctor F`,
this is the morphism from the preimage of `G` by `p` to `G`. -/
def fromPreimage (G : Subfunctor F) (p : F' ⟶ F) :
    (G.preimage p).toFunctor ⟶ G.toFunctor :=
  lift ((G.preimage p).ι ≫ p) (by
    rw [range_comp, range_ι, image_le_iff])

@[reassoc]
lemma fromPreimage_ι (G : Subfunctor F) (p : F' ⟶ F) :
    G.fromPreimage p ≫ G.ι = (G.preimage p).ι ≫ p := rfl

lemma preimage_eq_top_iff (G : Subfunctor F) (p : F' ⟶ F) :
    G.preimage p = ⊤ ↔ range p ≤ G := by
  rw [← image_top, image_le_iff]
  simp

@[simp]
lemma preimage_image_of_epi (G : Subfunctor F) (p : F' ⟶ F) [hp : Epi p] :
    (G.preimage p).image p = G := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · rw [image_le_iff]
  · intro i x hx
    simp only [NatTrans.epi_iff_epi_app, epi_iff_surjective] at hp
    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := hp _ x
    exact ⟨y, hx, rfl⟩

@[ext]
structure Subfunctor (F : C ⥤ Type w) where
  /-- If `G` is a subfunctor of `F`, then the sections of `G` on `U` forms a subset of sections of
  `F` on `U`. -/
  obj : ∀ U, Set (F.obj U)
  /-- If `G` is a subfunctor of `F` and `i : U ⟶ V`, then for each `G`-sections on `U` `x`,
  `F i x` is in `F(V)`. -/
  map : ∀ {U V : C} (i : U ⟶ V), obj U ⊆ F.map i ⁻¹' obj V

   153	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L

   190	/-! ## The two-way datum dictionary (the heart of GAP-6) -/
   191	
   192	/-- **The two-way fibre dictionary of the datum engine** (worksheet (V1b), stated at an
   193	arbitrary field of the test tower): for a pinned cocycle datum `D` over `S` and a field
   194	`L` in a `k`/`S`-tower, the engine's complex-form fibre condition
   195	`Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗[S] L)` holds iff the mapped class of the datum has a
   196	vanishing-`H¹` witness divisor over `L`.
   197	
   198	Forward: right-exactness (`subsingleton_h1_rTensor_iff`) makes the base-changed Čech
   199	differential surjective; the δ-naturality square (`datumDiffBaseChange`) carries
   200	surjectivity to the fibre datum's differential; `subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff`, the
   201	presentation bridge (`presentationSheafIso`) and the core isomorphism
   202	(`subsingleton_hModule_gluedSheaf_one_iff`) then read the vanishing on the witness
   203	`presentationDivisor` of the canonical subordinated presentation.  Backward: the landed
   204	seam `subsingleton_sheaf_h1_of_picClass_eq` + `subsingleton_h1_tensor_of_baseChange_sheaf`. -/
   205	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness
   206	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C S π) (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   207	    [Algebra S L] [IsScalarTower k S L] :
   208	    Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[S] L) ↔
   209	      ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
   210	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W
   211	            = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C S L) D.cechPicClass
   212	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   213	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1) := by
   214	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
   215	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
   216	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
   217	  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
   218	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
   219	  constructor
   220	  · intro h
   221	    -- surjectivity of the base-changed differential, through right-exactness
   222	    have hcok := ((datumPair D).subsingleton_h1_rTensor_iff L).mp h
   223	    have hbc : Function.Surjective ((datumPair D).diff.baseChange L) := by
   224	      rw [← LinearMap.range_eq_top]
   225	      exact Submodule.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mp hcok
   226	    -- across the δ-naturality square to the fibre datum's differential
   227	    have hsurj' : Function.Surjective (datumPair (D.baseChange L)).diff :=
   228	      RigidEngine.surjective_congr _ _ (D.datumDomBaseChange L)
   229	        (D.termBaseChangeInf L) (fun x => D.datumDiffBaseChange L x) hbc
   230	    haveI hH1L : Subsingleton (datumPair (D.baseChange L)).H1 := by
   231	      have himg : (datumPair (D.baseChange L)).imageLattice = ⊤ := by
   232	        rw [← (datumPair (D.baseChange L)).range_diff_eq, LinearMap.range_eq_top]
   233	        exact hsurj'
   234	      rw [TwoLatticePair.H1, himg]
   235	      infer_instance
   236	    have hsheaf : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange L).sheaf 1) :=
   237	      (subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff (D.baseChange L)).mp hH1L
   238	    -- the presentation bridge and the core isomorphism, on the canonical witness
   239	    set P : (relCurve C L).MeromorphicPresentation :=
   240	      Scheme.MeromorphicPresentation.ofCocycle (D.baseChange L).pointedCover
   241	        (gluedSubordCocycle (D.baseChange L).isGluingCocycle
   242	          (D.baseChange L).pointedCover (D.baseChange L).pieceIndex
   243	          fun _ => le_rfl) with hP
   244	    have hglued : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (P.gluedSheaf L) 1) :=
   245	      (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv (presentationSheafIso (D.baseChange L))
   246	        1).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mp hsheaf
   247	    have hdiv := (subsingleton_hModule_gluedSheaf_one_iff L P).mp hglued
   248	    refine ⟨Scheme.presentationDivisor L P, ?_, hdiv⟩
   249	    calc Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L (Scheme.presentationDivisor L P)
   250	        = P.picClass := Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor L P
   251	      _ = (D.baseChange L).cechPicClass := rfl
   252	      _ = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C S L) D.cechPicClass :=
   253	          D.cechPicClass_baseChange L
   254	  · rintro ⟨W, hW, hvan⟩
   255	    have hW' : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = (D.baseChange L).cechPicClass := by
   256	      rw [hW, D.cechPicClass_baseChange L]
   257	    exact D.subsingleton_h1_tensor_of_baseChange_sheaf L
   258	      (subsingleton_sheaf_h1_of_picClass_eq (D.baseChange L) hW' hvan)

    12	# DAT-C C2 — the rank-1 H⁰ export and the generator kit
    13	(`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` GAP-3 Σ-RANK1, §2 (N1)/(N3))
    14	
    15	On the fibrewise h¹-vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` with the base χ-normalization
    16	`χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`, the datum engine's `H⁰` is an **invertible** module: finite,
    17	projective, and of stalk-rank exactly `1`.  This is the rank export the engine
    18	(`datumRigidEngine`, `Cohomology/GluedSheafEngine.lean`) leaves open — it delivers
    19	finite + projective, never `rankAtStalk = 1`.
    20	
    21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_relCurve` — the χ transport `χ(𝒪_{C_L}) = 1 − n` to every
    22	  field `L` of the test tower (base-field invariance of the genus, `chi_moduleKSheaf`
    23	  + `genus_baseField`; a re-derivation of the private lemma of `DivSchemeMonoBridgeRel`).
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one` — **the fibre
    25	  computation**: for a datum whose fibre class over `L` has `classDeg = n`, with `H¹` of
    26	  the base-changed sheaf vanishing, `h⁰(C_L, F_{D_L}) = 1` — the Riemann–Roch anchor
    27	  `h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi` (`n + (1 − n)`) read through the presentation
    28	  bridge `presentationSheafIso`.  The fibre geometric package is threaded as instance
    29	  arguments (`Curve.BaseChangeInstances`).
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one` — **Σ-RANK1,
    31	  the datum-level export**: on the vanishing locus (fibre degree `n`, `χ = 1 − n`),
    32	  `Module.rankAtStalk (H⁰(F_D)) p = 1`.  Route: `Module.rankAtStalk_eq` reads the rank as
    33	  the `κ(p)`-fibre dimension; `datumH0BaseChange` (on the nose) identifies the fibre with
    34	  `H⁰(C_{κ(p)}, F_{D_{κ(p)}})`; the fibre computation above pins it at `1`.
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one` — the
    36	  certified-family specialization (**N1**): for `G` landing in the h¹-vanishing locus
    37	  `V`, the divisor datum `D_G := G.adaptation.divisorDatum` has invertible `H⁰`.  The
    38	  fibre-degree hypothesis is discharged uniformly by `DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass` (the
    39	  fibre class has `classDeg = n` at every field).
    40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily.exists_fibrewise_generator_divisorDatum`
    41	  — **N3, the generator kit**: since `H⁰(F_{D_G})` is projective of rank `1` (hence has a
    42	  nontrivial fibre at every prime of the locus), a fibrewise-nonzero **global** section

    92	      = 1 - (genus (baseChangeBundle C L) : ℤ) := chi_moduleKSheaf (baseChangeBundle C L)

    94	  have h3 : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (genus C : ℤ) := chi_moduleKSheaf C
    95	  have h4 : (genus C : ℤ) = (n : ℤ) := by rw [h3] at hχ; linarith

   139	/-- **Σ-RANK1, the datum-level rank export** (worksheet GAP-3): on the fibrewise
   140	h¹-vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` with the base χ-normalization `χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`,
   141	the datum engine's `H⁰` has stalk-rank exactly `1` at `p`.
   142	
   143	`Module.rankAtStalk_eq` reads the rank as the `κ(p)`-dimension of the fibre
   144	`κ(p) ⊗[S] H⁰`; the on-the-nose base change `datumH0BaseChange` identifies this fibre with
   145	`H⁰(C_{κ(p)}, F_{D_{κ(p)}})`, whose dimension is `1` by the fibre computation. The global
   146	fibrewise hypothesis `hfib` supplies finiteness/projectivity (hence flatness) through
   147	`datumRigidEngine`. -/
   148	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one
   149	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C S π) [IsNoetherianRing S]
   150	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   151	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   152	    (hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
   153	      Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   154	    (p : PrimeSpectrum S)
   155	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
   156	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   157	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   158	    [QuasiCompact
   159	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   160	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   161	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
   162	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   163	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)]
   164	    (hg : classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   165	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = (n : ℤ)) :
   166	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by

   169	  haveI := hproj
   170	  have hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1 := datum_subsingleton_pairH1 D hπ hfib
   171	  have hfibre : Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf = 1 :=
   172	    D.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one hχ p.asIdeal.ResidueField hg
   173	      (D.datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField hH1)
   174	  calc Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p
   175	      = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   176	          (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S] (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0)) :=
   177	        Module.rankAtStalk_eq p
   178	    _ = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   179	          (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf 0) :=
   180	        (D.datumH0BaseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField hH1).finrank_eq
   181	    _ = Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf := rfl

   191	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
   192	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1

   195	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]

   197	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]

    10	/-!
    11	# DAT-C C4 — the canonical-section normalization mono (N4/N5 + the local-basis companion)
    12	(`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §2 (N4)/(N5), GAP-3 companion)
    13	
    14	This file provides the module-theoretic heart of the canonical-section normalization —
    15	the deferred GAP-3 **Nakayama companion** (I-0253): a *given* fibrewise-nonzero element of
    16	a rank-`1` finite projective module is a **Zariski-local basis** (the converse direction
    17	of N3's generator production) — together with the DAT-A class law N4 for arbitrary
    18	fibrewise-regular sections of the divisor datum.
    19	
    20	* `Module.exists_notMem_bijective_toSpanSingleton` — **the Nakayama companion** (GAP-3
    21	  companion, deferred from C2/I-0253): for a finite projective `B`-module `Q` of
    22	  stalk-rank `1` at `p` and an element `q` nonzero in the fibre `Q ⊗ κ(p)`, there is a
    23	  basic open `D(f) ∋ p` on which `x ↦ x • q` is a **bijection** `B_f → Q_f`, i.e. `q`
    24	  is a local basis of `Q`.  Route: over the local ring `Rₚ` the localized module `Qₚ` is
    25	  free of rank `1`; the fibre nonzeroness pins the basis coordinate of `q` to a unit, so
    26	  `q` spans `Qₚ`; `PicardGroup`'s `bijective_of_surjective` (invertible target) upgrades
    27	  spanning to bijectivity, and `Module.FinitePresentation.exists_notMem_bijective` spreads
    28	  the stalk bijection to a basic open.
    29	* `Module.exists_notMem_smul_eq_of_tmul_ne_zero` — **the local-rescaling corollary** (the
    30	  N5 engine input): a second element `q'` lies in the `B_f`-span of the local basis `q`,
    31	  so `q' = a • q` in `Q_f` for a scalar `a`.
    32	
    33	Consumers: N5 (the relative uniqueness / mono engine) and the §3.2 chart mono
    34	consume the local basis to rescale the two canonical sections by a unit
    35	(the I-0231-safe route: invertibility of `H⁰`, never "fibrewise ⟹ relative").
    36	-/

    47	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] {Q : Type u} [AddCommGroup Q] [Module B Q]
    48	
    49	/-- **The Nakayama companion — a fibrewise-nonzero element is a Zariski-local basis**
    50	(worksheet GAP-3 companion, deferred from C2/I-0253): for a finite projective `B`-module
    51	`Q` of stalk-rank exactly `1` at the prime `p`, an element `q : Q` whose image in the
    52	fibre `Q ⊗ κ(p)` is nonzero generates `Q` freely on a basic open `D(f) ∋ p`: the map
    53	`x ↦ x • q` is a bijection `B_f → Q_f`.
    54	
    55	Over the local ring `Rₚ` the localized module `Qₚ` is free of rank `1`, so `q`'s basis
    56	coordinate `c` satisfies: if `c` were a non-unit it would lie in the maximal ideal, hence
    57	`q` would vanish in the fibre `κ(p) ⊗ Qₚ ≅ Q ⊗ κ(p)`, contradicting `hq`. Thus `c` is a
    58	unit and `q` spans `Qₚ`; `Module.Invertible`'s `bijective_of_surjective` promotes spanning
    59	to a bijection, and the isomorphism spreads to a basic open. -/
    60	theorem exists_notMem_bijective_toSpanSingleton
    61	    [Module.Finite B Q] [Module.Projective B Q] (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
    62	    (hrank : Module.rankAtStalk Q p = 1) (q : Q)
    63	    (hq : (q ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) : Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
    64	    ∃ f : B, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ Function.Bijective
    65	      (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers f) (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton B Q q)) := by
    66	  classical
    67	  haveI : Module.FinitePresentation B Q := Module.finitePresentation_of_projective B Q
    68	  set Rₚ := Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal with hRₚ
    69	  set Qₚ := LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q with hQₚ
    70	  set mkq : Qₚ := LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q q with hmkq
    71	  -- `Qₚ` is finite, flat and hence free of rank `1` over the local ring `Rₚ`
    72	  haveI : Module.Free Rₚ Qₚ := Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing
    73	  have hrank1 : Module.finrank Rₚ Qₚ = 1 := hrank
    74	  -- a basis of the free rank-`1` module, and the coordinate of `mkq`
    75	  set b : Module.Basis Unit Rₚ Qₚ := Module.basisUnique Unit hrank1 with hb
    76	  set c : Rₚ := b.repr mkq default with hc
    77	  have hmkq_eq : mkq = c • b default := by
    78	    have hsum := b.sum_repr mkq
    79	    rw [Fintype.sum_unique, ← hc] at hsum
    80	    exact hsum.symm
    81	  -- `c` is a unit: otherwise `mkq` vanishes in the fibre, contradicting `hq`
    82	  have hcunit : IsUnit c := by
    83	    rw [← IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal]
    84	    intro hcmem
    85	    -- the fibre map `κ ⊗[Rₚ] Qₚ → κ ⊗[B] Q` sends `1 ⊗ mkq` to `1 ⊗ q`, injectively
    86	    set κ := p.asIdeal.ResidueField with hκ
    87	    set η : Qₚ ≃ₗ[Rₚ] Rₚ ⊗[B] Q := LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q
    88	      with hη
    89	    set ε : κ ⊗[Rₚ] Qₚ →ₗ[Rₚ] κ ⊗[B] Q :=
    90	      (TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange B Rₚ κ κ Q).toLinearMap.restrictScalars Rₚ
    91	        ∘ₗ (η.lTensor κ).toLinearMap with hε
    92	    have hηmkq : η mkq = (1 : Rₚ) ⊗ₜ[B] q := by
    93	      rw [hη, hmkq, LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap_apply,
    94	        LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct_apply_mk, Localization.mk_one]
    95	    have hεval : ε ((1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[Rₚ] mkq) = (1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[B] q := by
    96	      simp only [hε, LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,
    97	        LinearEquiv.lTensor_tmul, hηmkq,
    98	        TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange_tmul, one_smul]
    99	    -- but `1 ⊗ mkq = 0` since `c ∈ maximalIdeal` kills the residue
   100	    have hcres : c • (1 : κ) = 0 := by
   101	      rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_one, IsLocalRing.ResidueField.algebraMap_eq]
   102	      exact (IsLocalRing.residue_eq_zero_iff c).mpr hcmem
   103	    have hzero : (1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[Rₚ] mkq = 0 := by
   104	      rw [hmkq_eq, ← TensorProduct.smul_tmul, hcres, TensorProduct.zero_tmul]
   105	    -- transport the vanishing to `Q ⊗ κ`, contradicting `hq`
   106	    have h1q : (1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[B] q = 0 := by rw [← hεval, hzero, map_zero]
   107	    exact hq (by
   108	      rw [show (q ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : κ) : Q ⊗[B] κ)
   109	          = TensorProduct.comm B κ Q ((1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[B] q) from rfl, h1q, map_zero])
   110	  -- `mkq` spans `Qₚ` (unit multiple of a basis element), so `toSpanSingleton` is surjective
   111	  haveI hinv : Module.Invertible Rₚ Qₚ :=
   112	    Module.Invertible.congr ((Module.nonempty_linearEquiv_of_finrank_eq_one hrank1).some)
   113	  have hspanmkq : Submodule.span Rₚ {mkq} = ⊤ := by
   114	    refine top_le_iff.mp ?_
   115	    rw [← b.span_eq, Set.range_unique, Submodule.span_le, Set.singleton_subset_iff,
   116	      SetLike.mem_coe]
   117	    refine Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mpr ⟨(hcunit.unit⁻¹ : Rₚˣ).val, ?_⟩
   118	    rw [hmkq_eq, smul_smul, hcunit.val_inv_mul, one_smul]
   119	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton Rₚ Qₚ mkq) := by
   120	    rw [← LinearMap.range_eq_top, LinearMap.range_toSpanSingleton]; exact hspanmkq
   121	  have hbijR : Function.Bijective (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton Rₚ Qₚ mkq) :=
   122	    Module.Invertible.bijective_of_surjective hsurj
   123	  -- identify the stalk of `toSpanSingleton` with `toSpanSingleton` over `Rₚ`
   124	  have hmapeq : IsLocalizedModule.map p.asIdeal.primeCompl (Algebra.linearMap B Rₚ)
   125	      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q) (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton B Q q)
   126	      = (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton Rₚ Qₚ mkq).restrictScalars B := by
   127	    refine IsLocalizedModule.ext p.asIdeal.primeCompl (Algebra.linearMap B Rₚ)
   128	      (IsLocalizedModule.map_units (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q)) ?_
   129	    refine LinearMap.ext fun x => ?_
   130	    rw [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply, IsLocalizedModule.map_apply]
   131	    simp only [LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply, LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply,
   132	      Algebra.linearMap_apply, map_smul, ← hmkq]
   133	    exact algebra_compatible_smul Rₚ x mkq
   134	  have hstalk : Function.Bijective (IsLocalizedModule.map p.asIdeal.primeCompl
   135	      (Algebra.linearMap B Rₚ) (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q)
   136	      (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton B Q q)) := by
   137	    rw [hmapeq]; exact hbijR
   138	  exact Module.FinitePresentation.exists_notMem_bijective (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton B Q q)
   139	    p.asIdeal (Algebra.linearMap B Rₚ)
   140	    (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q) hstalk
   141	
   142	/-- **The local-rescaling corollary** (the N5 engine input): with `q` a local basis at
   143	`p` (rank `1`, fibrewise nonzero), any second element `q'` lies in the `B_f`-span of `q`,
   144	so `q'` equals `a • q` in the away localization `Q_f` for a scalar `a : Localization.Away f`.
   145	This is the mechanism by which two fibrewise-nonzero sections of an invertible `H⁰` differ,
   146	Zariski-locally, by a scalar rescaling — and, when `q'` is itself fibrewise nonzero, by a
   147	**unit** rescaling (a `DivEq` move). -/
   148	theorem exists_notMem_smul_eq_of_tmul_ne_zero
   149	    [Module.Finite B Q] [Module.Projective B Q] (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
   150	    (hrank : Module.rankAtStalk Q p = 1) (q q' : Q)
   151	    (hq : (q ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) : Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
   152	    ∃ f : B, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ ∃ a : Localization.Away f,
   153	      (LocalizedModule.mk q' 1 : LocalizedModule.Away f Q) = a • LocalizedModule.mk q 1 := by
   154	  obtain ⟨f, hf, hbij⟩ := exists_notMem_bijective_toSpanSingleton p hrank q hq
   155	  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hbij.surjective (LocalizedModule.mk q' 1)
   156	  induction y using LocalizedModule.induction_on with
   157	  | h r s =>
   158	    refine ⟨f, hf, Localization.mk r s, ?_⟩
   159	    rw [← hy, LocalizedModule.mk_smul_mk, mul_one, LocalizedModule.map_mk,
   160	      LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply]
   161	
   162	end Module

    18	
    19	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionLocalEquations` — the LocalEquations datum of a

    21	  (the (1e) subordination interface `𝒲, σ, hσ`): equations the restricted components

    34	  rescalings and cover refinements of the constructed datum keep the class by the

    58	/-- The value of a restricted unit section is the restriction of its value. -/

    72	/-- The defining ratio equation of the section's restricted components on the overlaps

    74	from `⊤ ⊓ Uᵢ ⊓ Uⱼ`. -/
    75	private lemma component_ratio_eq (y y' : relCurve C B) :
    76	    ((relCurve C B).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
    77	        𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y' ≤ 𝒲.opens y)).op).hom
    78	        ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)))

    82	            𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y' ≤ 𝒲.opens y')).op).hom
    83	            ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y') (D.component s (σ y'))) := by
    84	  have hle : 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'
    85	      ≤ ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces (σ y) ⊓ D.pieces (σ y') :=
    86	    le_inf (le_inf le_top (inf_le_left.trans (hσ y))) (inf_le_right.trans (hσ y'))
    87	  have key := congrArg ((relCurve C B).resHom hle) (s.property (σ y) (σ y'))
    88	  rw [map_mul] at key
    89	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at key
    90	  change (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_left
    91	      ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)))
    92	    = (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :
    93	        Γ(relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'))
    94	      * (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_right
    95	          ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y') (D.component s (σ y')))
    96	  rw [gluedSubordUnit, val_unitsRestrict, component, component]
    97	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom]
    98	  exact key
    99	
   100	/-- **Sections ↦ divisor families** (DAT-A, worksheet §2.2 step 2): a germ-regular
   101	global section of the DAT-1 glued sheaf is a `Scheme.LocalEquations` datum on any
   102	pointed cover subordinated to the pieces — the equations are the (restricted)
   103	components, the ratio witnesses the subordinated transition units. Germ-regularity
   104	(`hreg`) is DAT-A2's output (`germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors` relatively;
   105	`Scheme.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero` on an integral field-level curve). -/
   106	noncomputable def sectionLocalEquations
   107	    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
   108	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
   109	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y)) :
   110	    (relCurve C B).LocalEquations where
   111	  cover := 𝒲
   112	  eqn y := (relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y))
   113	  regular y z hz := by
   114	    rw [Scheme.resHom, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
   115	    exact hreg (σ y) z (hσ y hz)
   116	  ratio_isUnit y y' :=
   117	    ⟨gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y', D.component_ratio_eq s 𝒲 σ hσ y y'⟩
   118	
   119	variable (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
   120	  ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
   121	    ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y))
   122	
   123	@[simp]
   124	lemma sectionLocalEquations_cover :
   125	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).cover = 𝒲 :=
   126	  rfl
   127	
   128	@[simp]
   129	lemma sectionLocalEquations_eqn (y : relCurve C B) :
   130	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).eqn y
   131	      = (relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)) :=
   132	  rfl
   133	
   134	/-- **The ratio units are exactly the cocycle's transition units** (worksheet §2.2 step
   135	2's "ratio units EXACTLY the cocycle"), in subordinated form: by uniqueness of ratio
   136	witnesses against a regular equation. On the piece cover the subordination is
   137	`≤`-reflexivity and `gluedSubordUnit` is the transition unit restricted along it. -/
   138	lemma sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit (y y' : relCurve C B) :
   139	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).ratioUnit y y'
   140	      = gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :=
   141	  ((D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).ratioUnit_unique y y'
   142	    (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y')
   143	    (D.component_ratio_eq s 𝒲 σ hσ y y')).symm
   144	
   145	/-- The units cocycle of the constructed LocalEquations datum is the (1e) subordinated
   146	cocycle of the datum. -/
   147	lemma sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle :
   148	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle
   149	      = gluedSubordCocycle D.isGluingCocycle 𝒲 σ hσ :=
   150	  Scheme.unitsCocycle_ext fun y y' =>
   151	    ((D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle_evInf y y').trans
   152	      ((D.sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg y y').trans
   153	        (gluedSubordCocycle_evInf D.isGluingCocycle 𝒲 σ hσ y y').symm)
   154	
   155	/-- **THE CLASS LAW** (DAT-A keystone; the Abel correspondence of worksheet §2.2 step
   156	2): the Picard class of the divisor datum cut out by a germ-regular global section of
   157	the DAT-1 glued sheaf is THE Čech Picard class of the datum's cocycle (stage (1e),
   158	consumed on the nose through `cechPicClass_eq_mk`). -/
   159	theorem sectionLocalEquations_picClass :
   160	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).picClass = D.cechPicClass := by
   161	  change Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒲
   162	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle.class = D.cechPicClass
   163	  rw [D.sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg]
   164	  exact D.cechPicClass_eq_mk 𝒲 σ hσ
   165	
   166	end AffineHom
   167	
   168	/-- **Independence of the section and the cover** (refinement/rescaling naturality,
   169	subsumed): the class of the divisor datum cut by ANY germ-regular section of the datum,
   170	on ANY subordinated pointed cover, is the same — both are `D.cechPicClass`. Unit
   171	rescalings and cover refinements of the constructed datum keep the class by the landed
   172	`LocalEquations.picClass_rescale`/`picClass_restrict`. -/
   173	theorem sectionLocalEquations_picClass_congr
   174	    {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
   175	    (s s' : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
   176	    (𝒲 𝒲' : (relCurve C B).PointedCover) (σ σ' : relCurve C B → D.index)
   177	    (hσ : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ y))
   178	    (hσ' : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲'.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ' y))
   179	    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
   180	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
   181	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y))
   182	    (hreg' : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
   183	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s' j)
   184	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y)) :
   185	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).picClass
   186	      = (D.sectionLocalEquations s' 𝒲' σ' hσ' hreg').picClass := by
   187	  rw [D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg,
   188	    D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s' 𝒲' σ' hσ' hreg']
   189	
   190	/-! ## The A2-bundled wrapper, on the canonical pointed cover -/
   191	
   192	section Bundled
   193	
   194	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
   195	variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
   196	
   197	/-- **Fibrewise-nonzero sections cut divisors** (DAT-A + DAT-A2, bundled): over a
   198	Noetherian test ring, a fibrewise-regular global section of the DAT-1 glued sheaf
   199	yields a `LocalEquations` divisor datum on the canonical pointed cover by pieces; its
   200	class is `D.cechPicClass` (`sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular_picClass`). -/
   201	noncomputable def sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular
   202	    [IsNoetherianRing B]
   203	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
   204	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
   205	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
   206	    (relCurve C B).LocalEquations :=
   207	  D.sectionLocalEquations s D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex (fun _ => le_rfl)
   208	    (fun j y hy => D.germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors s j (hfib j) y hy)
   209	
   210	/-- The class law for the A2-bundled wrapper: the fibrewise-regular section cuts a
   211	divisor of class exactly the datum's (1e) class. -/
   212	theorem sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular_picClass
   213	    [IsNoetherianRing B]
   214	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
   215	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
   216	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
   217	    (D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib).picClass = D.cechPicClass :=
   218	  D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex (fun _ => le_rfl) _
   219	
   220	end Bundled

     9	/-!
    10	# DAT-C C0 — the datum inverse, the divisor datum, and the canonical section
    11	(`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` GAP-1 + §2 (N2))
    12	
    13	Every landed datum built from a divisor family is the *twisted ideal* datum
    14	`𝒪(Θᵃ − d)` of class `θᵃ·[d]⁻¹` (G-0a). DAT-C's normalization layer needs a datum in
    15	the class `[𝒪(d)]` itself, together with its canonical section. This file pins both:
    16	
    17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.inv` — the **datum inverse**: same cover
    18	  data, transition units `(g i j)⁻¹`; the cocycle law inverts termwise.
    19	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.cechPicClass_inv` — the class law
    20	  `D.inv.cechPicClass = D.cechPicClass⁻¹` (subordinated-cocycle level).
    21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relThetaCocycle_zero`, `FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_zero`,
    22	  `thetaChartUnit_zero`, `cechPicClass_thetaChartDatum_zero` — at exponent `a = 0`
    23	  the theta twisting cocycle is trivial, so the whole-chart theta datum has class `1`
    24	  **over an arbitrary test ring** (the worksheet cites the base-`k` class law
    25	  `cechPicClass_thetaChartDatum` + `fiberTwist_zero`; the direct `a = 0` computation
    26	  is ring-generic, which the §2 consumers need — recorded deviation).
    27	* `DivisorAdaptation.divisorDatum` — **the divisor datum**
    28	  `(A.thetaIdealDatum 0).inv`, with class law
    29	  `cechPicClass_divisorDatum : A.divisorDatum.cechPicClass = d.picClass`
    30	  (G-0a at `a = 0` + the trivial theta block + `cechPicClass_inv`).
    31	* `DivisorAdaptation.canonSection` — **the canonical section is the equation system
    32	  itself** (N2): the components `(A.eqn j)` satisfy the inverse-datum matching
    33	  condition (`eqn_mul_eqnRatio` read against the inverted units), giving a global
    34	  section of the divisor datum's glued sheaf.
    35	* `DivisorAdaptation.divEq_sectionLocalEquations_canonSection` — **(N2) cut-back by
    36	  pure refinement**: the `LocalEquations` datum cut by `canonSection` (DAT-A
    37	  `sectionLocalEquations`, on any subordinated pointed cover) is `DivEq` to `d` —
    38	  the comparison units are the adaptation's own `eqn_rel` units; no fibre argument.
    39	-/
    40

    42	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    43	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
