    57	/-! ## The datum inverse -/
    58	
    59	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
    60	
    61	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
    62	
    63	/-- The pair value of an inverse unit cocycle is the inverse pair value. -/
    64	private lemma inv_unitsEvInf {X : Scheme.{u}} {𝒰 : X.PointedCover}
    65	    (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (i j : X) :
    66	    Scheme.unitsEvInf γ⁻¹ i j = (Scheme.unitsEvInf γ i j)⁻¹ := rfl
    67	
    68	/-- The unit-level cocycle identity of a datum (the value-level law `mul_res`
    69	re-packaged through `Units.ext`). -/
    70	private lemma unitsRestrict_unit_mul (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
    71	    (i j l : D.index) :
    72	    (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict
    73	        (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ⊓ D.pieces l ≤ D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)
    74	        (D.unit i j)
    75	      * (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict (gluedInclCoc D.pieces (D.pieces i) j l)
    76	          (D.unit j l)
    77	      = (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict (gluedInclSnd D.pieces (D.pieces i) j l)
    78	          (D.unit i l) :=
    79	  Units.ext (D.isGluingCocycle.mul_res i j l)
    80	
    81	/-- **The datum inverse** (worksheet GAP-1): the same basic-open cover data with the
    82	termwise-inverted transition units `(g i j)⁻¹`. The cocycle law inverts termwise —
    83	the units are honest `Units`, and the section rings are commutative. -/
    84	noncomputable def inv (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) :
    85	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π where
    86	  toBasicOpenCoverData := D.toBasicOpenCoverData
    87	  unit i j := (D.unit i j)⁻¹
    88	  isGluingCocycle := by
    89	    constructor
    90	    · intro i
    91	      rw [show D.unit i i = 1 from Units.ext (D.isGluingCocycle.unit_self i), inv_one,
    92	        Units.val_one]
    93	    · intro i j l
    94	      have key : ((relCurve C B).unitsRestrict
    95	            (inf_le_left :
    96	              D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ⊓ D.pieces l ≤ D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)
    97	            (D.unit i j))⁻¹
    98	          * ((relCurve C B).unitsRestrict (gluedInclCoc D.pieces (D.pieces i) j l)
    99	              (D.unit j l))⁻¹
   100	          = ((relCurve C B).unitsRestrict (gluedInclSnd D.pieces (D.pieces i) j l)
   101	              (D.unit i l))⁻¹ := by
   102	        rw [← mul_inv]
   103	        exact congrArg (·⁻¹) (D.unitsRestrict_unit_mul i j l)
   104	      have hval := congrArg Units.val key
   105	      rw [Units.val_mul] at hval
   106	      exact hval
   107	
   108	@[simp]
   109	lemma inv_pieces (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) : D.inv.pieces = D.pieces := rfl
   110	
   111	@[simp]
   112	lemma inv_unit (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (i j : D.index) :
   113	    D.inv.unit i j = (D.unit i j)⁻¹ := rfl
   114	
   115	/-- **The class law of the datum inverse**: `[D⁻¹] = [D]⁻¹`. Both classes are computed
   116	by subordinated cocycles on `D`'s canonical pointed cover by pieces, where the
   117	subordinated cocycle of the inverse datum is the inverse cocycle. -/
   118	theorem cechPicClass_inv (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) :
   119	    D.inv.cechPicClass = D.cechPicClass⁻¹ := by
   120	  have hσ : ∀ x : relCurve C B,
   121	      D.pointedCover.opens x ≤ D.inv.pieces (D.pieceIndex x) :=
   122	    fun _ => le_rfl
   123	  have hco : gluedSubordCocycle D.inv.isGluingCocycle D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex hσ
   124	      = (gluedSubordCocycle D.isGluingCocycle D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
   125	          (fun _ => le_rfl))⁻¹ := by
   126	    refine Scheme.unitsCocycle_ext fun x y => ?_
   127	    rw [gluedSubordCocycle_evInf, inv_unitsEvInf, gluedSubordCocycle_evInf]
   128	    exact Units.ext rfl
   129	  calc D.inv.cechPicClass
   130	      = Scheme.CechPic.mk D.pointedCover
   131	          (gluedSubordCocycle D.inv.isGluingCocycle D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
   132	            hσ).class :=
   133	        (D.inv.cechPicClass_eq_mk D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex hσ).symm
   134	    _ = Scheme.CechPic.mk D.pointedCover
   135	          ((gluedSubordCocycle D.isGluingCocycle D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
   136	            (fun _ => le_rfl)).class)⁻¹ := by
   137	        rw [hco, OneCocycle.class_inv]
   138	    _ = D.cechPicClass⁻¹ := rfl
   139	
   140	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

   142	/-! ## The theta block is trivial at exponent zero -/
   143	
   144	section ThetaZero
   145	
   146	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
   147	
   148	/-- The relative theta cocycle at exponent `0` is the trivial unit: `t₀⁰ = 1`. -/
   149	theorem relThetaCocycle_zero : relThetaCocycle C B π 0 = 1 := by
   150	  change relUnitCocycle C B (fiberTwoCover π) (thetaUnit π ^ 0) = 1
   151	  rw [pow_zero]
   152	  exact map_one _
   153	
   154	/-- The theta twisting units of a finite cover datum are trivial at exponent `0`. -/
   155	theorem FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_zero (D : FinCoverData C B π) (i j : D.index) :
   156	    D.thetaOvlUnit 0 i j = 1 := by
   157	  rcases i with i | i <;> rcases j with j | j
   158	  · rfl
   159	  · rw [FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_inl_inr, relThetaCocycle_zero, map_one]
   160	  · rw [FinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_inr_inl, relThetaCocycle_zero, map_one, inv_one]
   161	  · rfl
   162	
   163	/-- The whole-chart theta transition units are trivial at exponent `0`. -/
   164	theorem thetaChartUnit_zero (i j : (thetaChartCover C B π).index) :
   165	    thetaChartUnit C B π 0 i j = 1 := by
   166	  rcases i with i | i <;> rcases j with j | j
   167	  · rfl
   168	  · change (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict _ (relThetaCocycle C B π 0) = 1
   169	    rw [relThetaCocycle_zero, map_one]
   170	  · change (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict _ (relThetaCocycle C B π 0)⁻¹ = 1
   171	    rw [relThetaCocycle_zero, inv_one, map_one]
   172	  · rfl
   173	
   174	/-- **The whole-chart theta datum has trivial class at exponent `0`, over an arbitrary
   175	test ring**: all its transition units are `1`, so the subordinated cocycle is the
   176	trivial cocycle. (Ring-generic strengthening of the base-`k` route
   177	`cechPicClass_thetaChartDatum` + `fiberTwist_zero`.) -/
   178	theorem cechPicClass_thetaChartDatum_zero :
   179	    (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).cechPicClass = 1 := by
   180	  have hco : gluedSubordCocycle (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).isGluingCocycle
   181	      (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pointedCover (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pieceIndex
   182	      (fun _ => le_rfl) = 1 := by
   183	    refine Scheme.unitsCocycle_ext fun x y => ?_
   184	    rw [gluedSubordCocycle_evInf, Scheme.one_unitsEvInf]
   185	    change (relCurve C B).unitsRestrict _
   186	        (thetaChartUnit C B π 0 ((thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pieceIndex x)
   187	          ((thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pieceIndex y)) = 1
   188	    rw [thetaChartUnit_zero, map_one]
   189	  change Scheme.CechPic.mk (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pointedCover
   190	      (gluedSubordCocycle (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).isGluingCocycle
   191	        (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pointedCover (thetaChartDatum C B π 0).pieceIndex
   192	        (fun _ => le_rfl)).class = 1
   193	  rw [hco, OneCocycle.class_one, Scheme.CechPic.mk_one]
   194	
   195	end ThetaZero

   197	/-! ## The divisor datum and its class law -/
   198	
   199	namespace DivisorAdaptation
   200	
   201	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
   202	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
   203	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
   204	
   205	/-- The ideal transition units at exponent `0` are the plain ratio units `f_j/f_i`:
   206	the theta block is trivial. -/
   207	theorem thetaIdealUnit_zero (i j : A.index) :
   208	    A.thetaIdealUnit 0 i j = A.eqnRatio i j := by
   209	  rw [thetaIdealUnit, A.toFinCoverData.thetaOvlUnit_zero, mul_one]
   210	
   211	/-- **The divisor datum of an adaptation** (worksheet GAP-1): the inverse of the
   212	twisted ideal datum at exponent `0` — a pinned cocycle datum in the class `[𝒪(d)]`
   213	(`cechPicClass_divisorDatum`), whose transition units are the inverted ratio units
   214	`(f_j/f_i)⁻¹`. -/
   215	noncomputable def divisorDatum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C R π :=
   216	  (A.thetaIdealDatum 0).inv
   217	
   218	/-- **The class law of the divisor datum**: `[divisorDatum] = [𝒪(d)]` — G-0a at
   219	`a = 0`, the trivial theta block, and the class law of the datum inverse. -/
   220	theorem cechPicClass_divisorDatum : A.divisorDatum.cechPicClass = d.picClass := by
   221	  change (A.thetaIdealDatum 0).inv.cechPicClass = d.picClass
   222	  rw [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.cechPicClass_inv, A.cechPicClass_thetaIdealDatum 0,
   223	    cechPicClass_thetaChartDatum_zero, one_mul, inv_inv]
   224	
   225	/-! ### The canonical section -/
   226	
   227	/-- The value-level matching law of the equation components against the inverted ratio

     8	/-!
     9	# THE PRODUCER: `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` for a class in the image of the sheafification unit
    10	
    11	## What this file closes
    12	
    13	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean` proves CHART-U(b) at a general test from a per-affine-piece
    14	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, and its header says plainly what it does not do:
    15	
    16	> The hypothesis is a *per-affine-piece existence of a datum with the plus-class property*, and
    17	> nothing here produces such a datum.
    18	
    19	**This file produces one**, and the ingredient that was missing is smaller than four successive
    20	sessions on this leaf priced it: on an **affine** test the canonical field point `Over.testPoint t`
    21	**is** the base-change morphism `overSpecMap A κ(t)`.  Both sides are `Spec` of the same ring map —
    22	`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine` is *defined* as `Spec.preimage` of `fromSpecResidueField`,
    23	so `Spec.map_preimage` closes it — but nothing in the tree said so, and every plus-class identity
    24	on this lane is an identity between a class pulled along `Over.testPoint` and one pulled along
    25	`relCurveMap`.  Without the comparison the two sides are not even syntactically comparable; with
    26	it they are the same class.
    27	
    28	## The shape of the producer, and its one genuine restriction
    29	
    30	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D` compares `μ`'s fibre at `κ(t)`, read as a plus class, with the
    31	plus-*unit* of `D`'s fibre class.  So the natural hypothesis on `μ` is that it is *already* a
    32	plus unit — i.e. in the image of the sheafification unit `relPicToPicEt` — and then `D` comes
    33	from `exists_cechPicClass_eq` applied to any Čech representative.
    34	
    35	That restriction is real and is named `IsPlusHonest` below.  It is **not** vacuous and **not**
    36	automatic:
    37	
    38	* not automatic — a general plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`,
    39	  and `Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is precisely the record that it becomes honest only over
    40	  `E.Carrier`, not over `A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is a genuine hypothesis, not a restatement;
    41	* not vacuous, and this is the payoff — the range of `relPicToPicEt` is a **subgroup**, and every
    42	  class the chart layer twists by is in it: the θ-family (`thetaFamily_isPlusHonest`), the
    43	  Σ-family, and the Abel value itself (`abelDiv_isPlusHonest`).  So `chartTwist` preserves
    44	  honesty, and CHART-U(b) becomes **unconditional** on exactly the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart reads.
    45	
    46	  **A CORRECTION TO THIS PARAGRAPH, from a fresh-context review of the commit that first wrote
    47	  it, and it is the same failure this leaf recorded one round earlier.**  When first committed the
    48	  sentence above cited `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` **and that declaration did not exist** — a
    49	  workspace-wide grep returned exactly one hit, the sentence itself.  That is precisely the
    50	  failure mode r7 diagnosed (`docstring-declaration-lists-unchecked`) and filed a lesson about,
    51	  reproduced by the very session that filed it, inside its own *non-vacuity* argument.
    52	  A kernel check, a `sorry` census and an axiom probe are all silent about it.
    53	
    54	  It also mattered mathematically, which is why it was worth writing rather than deleting: the
    55	  θ- and Σ-witnesses are the **twist factors**, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest` discharges anyway,
    56	  so they say nothing about the class being *charted*.  Since `chartValue = abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹`,
    57	  honesty of a chart value reduces to honesty of `abelDiv` alone — so `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` was
    58	  carrying the whole of the final clause.  It is now proved (below), so the paragraph stands as
    59	  written; had it not been, the honest statement would have been "no residue beyond
    60	  `IsPlusHonest lam`", with the Σ-chart clause unproved.
    61	
    62	## Main declarations
    63	
    64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.testPoint_eq_overSpecMap` — **the comparison**: on an affine test the
    65	  canonical field point is the base-change morphism.
    66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt` — the producer, with the datum given.
    67	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range` — **the producer proper**: for a
    68	  class in the image of the unit, a datum with the plus-class property EXISTS.
    69	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsPlusHonest` — the per-affine-piece form, closed under the group operations.
    70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest` — **CHART-U(b) with no residue** for an
    71	  honest class, and `chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest` the same open as DATA.
    72	-/

     8	/-!
     9	# A plus class becomes honest over its own étale carrier — over an ARBITRARY affine base
    10	
    11	This closes the obligation the CHART-U(b) header table names "honesty over a general affine
    12	base" (issue I-0558), and it needs no field.
    13	
    14	## The obligation, and why it looked hard
    15	
    16	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean`'s route needs a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over an affine base
    17	whose class is the (collapsed) twisted class.  `exists_datum_cechPicClass_chartTwistClass`
    18	(`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistCollapse.lean`) supplies the datum — but it takes an **honest Čech
    19	class** `c` over the base as a *hypothesis*, and a plus class over `Spec A` is not honest: it is
    20	`PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E` of `A`.
    21	
    22	The tree's only route from a plus class to an honest one was
    23	`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`'s `exists_splitting_of_picEt`, which requires `[Field K]` — its
    24	engine is étale field-cofinality (`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`),
    25	false over a general base.  So the obligation read as: find a *substitute* for cofinality over
    26	`Spec A`.
    27	
    28	## Why it is in fact free
    29	
    30	There is no substitute needed, because **a cover splits over its own carrier**.  The
    31	field-cofinality theorem is used to produce an `A`-algebra map `E.Carrier →ₐ L` into something
    32	where the class becomes a unit; but the identity `E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier` is already such a
    33	map, and it exists for every cover over every base.  Restricting the plus class along
    34	`A → E.Carrier` therefore makes it honest, with no finiteness, separability, or field
    35	hypothesis anywhere.
    36	
    37	Concretely `PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (PicEtAff.mk C E x) = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier x` — the
    38	transported class is presented by `x` itself.  The proof is the general-base analogue of
    39	`PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom` (`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:79`), which is stated
    40	only for fields; the field hypotheses there are inherited from *its* consumer (the degree seam,
    41	which reads a degree and so needs a field), not required by the argument.  The one substantive
    42	step is the same in both: the descent condition `x.2`, fed to `relPicAlgMap_congr`, identifies
    43	the two ways of transporting `x` to the base-changed carrier.
    44	
    45	## What this does and does not give
    46	
    47	It gives honesty **over `Spec E.Carrier`**, not over `Spec A`.  That is exactly what the
    48	(b-amendment) asks for — its step is "over the étale carrier `B := E.Carrier` the class is
    49	honest", after which the engine fires on `Spec B` and transport (ii) pushes the open locus down
    50	to `Spec A` along the (open, surjective) carrier map.  Nothing here performs that descent; the
    51	topological core of it is landed as `isOpen_of_isOpen_comap_preimage`
    52	(`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusOpen.lean:129`).
    53	
    54	So after this file the CHART-U(b) route has ONE remaining obligation, the pointwise
    55	`IsChartDatumPresentation` — and, unlike the previous "one remaining obligation" claims on this
    56	lane, that one is a genuine statement about matching two fibre predicates, not a missing
    57	construction.
    58	
    59	## Main declarations
    60	
    61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self` — **a plus class is honest over its own
    62	  cover carrier**, over an arbitrary affine base.
    63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_honest_of_picEtAff` — the existential form.
    64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_datum_cechPicClass_twist` — the payoff, in the engine's shape: over
    65	  a base where the class is honest, a datum presenting it twisted by any chart index exists.
    66	-/

    99	
   100	`PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (PicEtAff.mk C E x) = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier x`: the class
   101	presented by `x` on the cover `E` restricts, along `A → E.Carrier`, to the tautological plus
   102	unit of `x` itself.
   103	
   104	This is the general-base analogue of `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom`
   105	(`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:79`) at `ℓ := AlgHom.id`.  That lemma carries `[Field K]`,

   120	  refine congrArg (PicEtAff.mk C (E.baseChange E.Carrier)) (Subtype.ext ?_)

   122	  exact relPicAlgMap_congr C (E.baseChangeInclude E.Carrier)
   123	    ((Algebra.ofId E.Carrier (E.baseChange E.Carrier).Carrier).restrictScalars A) x.2

   127	/-- **Every plus class over an affine base is honest over some affine base above it** — the

   136	theorem exists_honest_of_picEtAff {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   137	    (a : PicEtAff C A) :
   138	    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra k B) (_ : Algebra A B)
   139	        (_ : IsScalarTower k A B) (z : relPic C (overSpec k B)),

   144	      (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)), ?_⟩
   145	    exact PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self C E x

   150	/-- **The engine input, assembled**: for any plus class over any affine base `A` and any chart

   152	a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `B` presenting `c` twisted by the chart index exists.
   153	
   154	This composes the two halves that were previously recorded as separate gates:
   155	
   156	* honesty over `B := E.Carrier` — `exists_honest_of_picEtAff` above, which needs no field;
   157	* presentation of the twisted class by a datum — `exists_cechPicClass_eq`, applied at the
   158	  *product* class, which is why no `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.mul` is needed
   159	  (`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistCollapse.lean`).

   161	The conclusion is exactly the input of
   162	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing`, so the openness of the witness
   163	locus over `Spec B` is available for every plus class and every chart index.  What is *not* here

   167	Stated with `c` as a hypothesis rather than bundled into the existential: bundling it forces the

By the criterion that the right adjoint of a mono-preserving left adjoint preserves injectives (Lemma 209), each \(j_*\mathcal{I}^n\) is injective in \(X.\mathrm{Modules}\). An injective object is right-\(G\)-acyclic for any additive functor \(G\) (Lemma 152, in the sense of Definition 155), so \(j_*\mathcal{I}^n\) is \(f_*\)-acyclic: \(R^k f_*(j_*\mathcal{I}^n) = 0\) for all \(k \geq 1\). /-!
# The category of sheaves of modules over a scheme

In this file, we define the abelian category of sheaves of modules
`X.Modules` over a scheme `X`, and study its basic functoriality.

-/

@[expose] public section

universe t u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace SheafOfModules Bicategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

variable {X Y Z T : Scheme.{u}}

variable (X) in
/-- The category of sheaves of modules over a scheme. -/
def Modules := SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf

namespace Modules

/-- Morphisms between `𝒪ₓ`-modules. Use `Hom.app` to act on sections. -/
def Hom (M N : X.Modules) : Type u := SheafOfModules.Hom M N

instance : Category X.Modules where
  Hom := Modules.Hom
  __ := (inferInstance : Category (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf))

noncomputable instance : Abelian X.Modules :=
  inferInstanceAs <| Abelian (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)
instance : HasLimits X.Modules := inferInstanceAs (HasLimits (SheafOfModules X.ringCatSheaf))
instance : HasColimits X.Modules := inferInstanceAs (HasColimits (SheafOfModules X.ringCatSheaf))

section Functor

variable (X) in
/-- The forgetful functor from `𝒪ₓ`-modules to presheaves of modules.
This is mostly useful to transport results from (pre)sheaves of modules to `𝒪ₓ`-modules and
usually shouldn't be used directly when working with actual `𝒪ₓ`-modules. -/
def toPresheafOfModules : X.Modules ⥤ X.PresheafOfModules := SheafOfModules.forget _

/-- The forgetful functor from `𝒪ₓ`-modules to presheaves of modules is fully faithful. -/
def fullyFaithfulToPresheafOfModules : (Modules.toPresheafOfModules X).FullyFaithful :=
  SheafOfModules.fullyFaithfulForget _

instance : (toPresheafOfModules X).Full := fullyFaithfulToPresheafOfModules.full
instance : (toPresheafOfModules X).Faithful := fullyFaithfulToPresheafOfModules.faithful
instance : (toPresheafOfModules X).IsRightAdjoint :=
  (PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).isRightAdjoint

variable (X) in
/-- The forgetful functor from `𝒪ₓ`-modules to presheaves of abelian groups. -/
noncomputable def toPresheaf : X.Modules ⥤ TopCat.Presheaf Ab X :=
  toPresheafOfModules X ⋙ PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _

instance : (toPresheaf X).Faithful := .comp _ (PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _)
instance : PreservesLimits (toPresheaf X) := comp_preservesLimits _ (PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _)
instance : (toPresheaf X).ReflectsIsomorphisms :=
  reflectsIsomorphisms_comp _ (PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _)

end Functor

variable {M N K : X.Modules} {φ : M ⟶ N} {U V : X.Opens}

section Presheaf

/-- The underlying abelian presheaf of an `𝒪ₓ`-module. -/
noncomputable def presheaf (M : X.Modules) : TopCat.Presheaf Ab X := M.1.presheaf

/-- Notation for sections of a presheaf of module. -/
scoped[AlgebraicGeometry] notation3 "Γ(" M ", " U ")" => (Scheme.Modules.presheaf M).obj (.op U)

instance : Module Γ(X, U) Γ(M, U) := (M.val.obj (.op U)).isModule

variable (M) in
@[simp] lemma map_smul (i : U ⟶ V) (r : Γ(X, V)) (x : Γ(M, V)) :
    M.presheaf.map i.op (r • x) = X.presheaf.map i.op r • M.presheaf.map i.op x :=
  M.val.map_smul _ _ _

/-- Scalar multiplication as an endomorphism of `Γ(M, U)`. -/
def smul : Γ(X, U) →+* End Γ(M, U) :=
  (M.val.obj (.op U)).smul

@[simp]
lemma smul_apply (r : Γ(X, U)) (x : Γ(M, U)) : (M.smul r).hom x = r • x := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma map_comp_smul (i : U ⟶ V) (r : Γ(X, V)) :
    M.smul r ≫ M.presheaf.map i.op = M.presheaf.map i.op ≫ M.smul (X.presheaf.map i.op r) := by
  ext
  simp

/-- The underlying map between abelian presheaves of a morphism of `𝒪ₓ`-modules. -/
noncomputable def Hom.mapPresheaf (φ : M ⟶ N) : M.presheaf ⟶ N.presheaf :=
  (toPresheaf X).map φ

/-- The application of a morphism of `𝒪ₓ`-modules to sections. -/
def Hom.app (φ : M ⟶ N) (U : X.Opens) : Γ(M, U) ⟶ Γ(N, U) :=
  (forget₂ _ _).map (φ.val.app (.op U))

@[simp] lemma mapPresheaf_app (φ : M ⟶ N) (U) : φ.mapPresheaf.app U = φ.app U.unop := rfl

@[simp]
lemma Hom.app_smul (φ : M ⟶ N) (r : Γ(X, U)) (x : Γ(M, U)) :
    φ.app U (r • x) = r • φ.app U x :=
  (φ.val.app (.op U)).hom.map_smul r x

@[simp] lemma Hom.add_app (φ ψ : M ⟶ N) : (φ + ψ).app U = φ.app U + ψ.app U := rfl
@[simp] lemma Hom.sub_app (φ ψ : M ⟶ N) : (φ - ψ).app U = φ.app U - ψ.app U := rfl
@[simp] lemma Hom.zero_app : (0 : M ⟶ N).app U = 0 := rfl
@[simp] lemma Hom.id_app (M : X.Modules) : (𝟙 M :).app U = 𝟙 _ := rfl
@[simp] lemma Hom.comp_app (φ : M ⟶ N) (ψ : N ⟶ K) : (φ ≫ ψ).app U = φ.app U ≫ ψ.app U := rfl

@[ext]
lemma hom_ext (f g : M ⟶ N) (H : ∀ U, f.app U = g.app U) : f = g := by
  apply SheafOfModules.hom_ext
  ext U x
  exact congr($(H U.unop) x)

lemma isSheaf (M : X.Modules) : M.presheaf.IsSheaf := SheafOfModules.isSheaf M

@[simp] lemma toPresheaf_obj : (toPresheaf X).obj M = M.presheaf := rfl
@[simp] lemma toPresheaf_map : (toPresheaf X).map φ = φ.mapPresheaf := rfl

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
lemma Hom.isIso_iff_isIso_app {M N : X.Modules} {φ : M ⟶ N} :
    IsIso φ ↔ ∀ U, IsIso (φ.app U) := by
  rw [← isIso_iff_of_reflects_iso _ (toPresheaf X), NatTrans.isIso_iff_isIso_app]
  simp [Opposite.op_surjective.forall]

instance [IsIso φ] : IsIso (φ.app U) := Hom.isIso_iff_isIso_app.mp ‹_› _

@[simp, push ←]
lemma inv_app [IsIso φ] : (inv φ).app U = inv (φ.app U) := by
  apply IsIso.eq_inv_of_hom_inv_id
  simp [← Hom.comp_app]

end Presheaf

lemma pushforward_obj_obj (M : X.Modules) (U : Y.Opens) :
